Short version: Ntoma works on your phone. We only send an image somewhere when you ask for AI generation, and we say so when it happens.
Fabric photos you capture or pick, and — only if you use try-on — one photo of a person. Generated looks are stored in the app\'s private storage.

On-device analysis: no. Your fabric photo is analysed on the phone and never uploaded. Cloud analysis and AI try-on: yes — the image is sent to the configured backend so the model can process it. The engine in use is always shown on the analysis screen.
Locally, until you delete them. A connected backend decides its own retention; we recommend a maximum of 24 hours for uploaded images, and the demo engine keeps nothing.
How do I delete my data?
Use Delete my data below. It removes scans, analyses, looks, history, favourites and cached images from this device immediately.
This build ships with a debug-only logger. No analytics SDK is included and no usage data leaves your device.

This version of Ntoma contains no advertisements and no advertising SDK. No advertising identifiers or ad data are collected. If ads are introduced in a future version, they will be clearly labelled and this policy will be updated first.

Camera (only when you scan or take a photo) and notifications (only if you enable them). Photos are read through the Android photo picker, so no storage permission is requested. We never ask for contacts, location, microphone, SMS, phone or call logs.
This permanently removes your fabrics, analyses, generated looks, history and favourites from this device. It cannot be undone.
Your local data has been deleted

Ntoma helps you explore how a fabric could look as a garment. Suggestions and visualisations are ideas, not professional tailoring advice, and results depend on your fabric, measurements and seamstress.
You keep the rights to the photos you upload. You are responsible for having permission to use any photo of another person, and for how you share generated images.
Generated images are illustrative. Do not present them as a finished garment, a guarantee of fit, or a real photograph of an existing product.
The service is provided as-is during beta. Premium features in this build are not connected to billing, and no payment is collected.
Contact support to report a problem or to request removal of your data.

Ntoma — “cloth” in Akan. Built with Jetpack Compose. Fabric and style knowledge draws on Ghanaian dress traditions including kente, adinkra, wax print and the smock. All demo imagery in this build is generated from your own fabric colours; no third-party photographs are bundled.
1. Scan or upload a fabric photo.
2. Read the analysis: colours, pattern, texture and a possible Ghanaian style.
3. Browse matching designs for women and men, filtered by occasion.
4. Optionally preview a design on a photo of a person.
5. Save what you like and share it with your tailor.
Fill the frame with the print, use daylight, keep the cloth flat, and avoid strong shadows or flash glare.

Is the try-on a real fitting?
No. It shows colour and scale on a person. Fit and finish depend on your tailor.

Not yet. The style library is loaded from a catalogue that can be updated from the backend.
